source_latex: {Let $\tilde{\bm x}$ be an approximate solution of linear systems \eqref{eq:linear-system}. Then a quantitative way to know the distance between the solution $\bm x$ and the approximate solution $\tilde{\bm x}$ is to compute a vector norm of $\bm x-\tilde{\bm x}$. Further, a quantitative way to measure the distance between two matrices $A,B$ is given by a matrix norm of $A-B$. The definitions of a vector norm and a matrix norm are described in the next two subsections. The explanations are based on \BookCite{170}, and for the details of numerical linear algebra, see \BookCite{45}, \BookCite{79}, \BookCite{107}, \BookCite{191}.}
